title: Eternal Source of Life and Light
description: Eternal Source of Life and Light in Tonic Solfa to ST. PETER, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 81 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Prayer for Divine Direction”, where the book credits them to Cappe's Selection.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. PETER; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: E-ter-nal Source of life and light, Su-preme-ly good and wise, To thee we bring our grate-ful vows, To thee lift up our eyes.

lines: Eternal Source of life and light,
To thee we bring our grateful vows,
To thee lift up our eyes.
Our dark and erring minds illume
Inspire our hearts with sacred love,
And tune our lips to praise.
Safely conduct us, by thy grace,
And place us, when that journey's o'er
At thy right hand, O God.

licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1853.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST. PETER by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
